newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar content to sit still, ends unchanged.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar content to sit still, ends unchanged.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar spent a very quiet Monday session in a narrow range and traders are anticipating settled trading through the week.
It ended at 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) at US$0.6759/66, having traded in just a seven basis point range. The long holiday weekend in the U.S. affected the depth of the market.
The Trade-Weighted Index closed down at 66.15 from its 66.41 opening as it responded to dollar/yen weakness.
Dealers said there was reasonable Asian buying interest as players chased higher New Zealand cash rates, but the buyers found ready sellers.

The downside for the kiwi is seen as limited after the Reserve Bank said on Thursday it was unhappy at how far conditions had eased. A support base for the kiwi was seen at 0.6750, depending on the strength or weakness of the TWI.
But there are plenty of sellers keen to bail out at the figure, dealers said.
Other than March quarter balance of payments data on Friday, there is little until next week's CPI to drive the market, which dealers said would encourage stability.
